name: Belgian Dutch (Flemish)
notes: Flemish / Belgian Dutch (Vlaams). Alveolar /r/ [r] in most varieties (vs. NL uvular [ʀ]). /ɣ/ (voiced velar fricative) more robust than in NL Dutch. Considered more conservative than Netherlands Dutch in some features. Strong dialect continuum from West-Flemish to Limburgish. Source: König & van der Auwera (1994). ⟨w⟩ (Verhoeven 2005, JIPA 35(2)): "[w] has a labial-velar articulation rather than labiodental in many accents of Netherlandic Dutch" (p. 245), with "w waːʀ̥ waar 'true'" in the word list (p. 244). So ⟨w⟩ is [w], against the [ʋ] of nl-NL, and the consonant that ⟨ieuw eeuw uw⟩ give before a vowel is [w] too: leeuwen [leːwən], nieuwe [niwə], duwen [dywən]. Paardekooper (1987, ABN-uitspraakgids, p. XVIII) notes the same bilabial w "in veel zuidelijke dialecten".
